QUESTION: Let $F_t$ be the characteristic functional of the loop $\texttt{while}(\varphi)\{c\}$ with respect to continuation $t$. Suppose a runtime $I$ satisfies $F_t(I) \le I$. What can be concluded about $\mathrm{ert}[\texttt{while}(\varphi)\{c\}](t)$ and the runtime $I$?

ATOM: If a runtime $I$ is an upper invariant of the loop $\texttt{while}(\varphi)\{c\}$ with respect to continuation $t$, i.e. a pre-fixed point satisfying $F_t(I) \le I$, then $\mathrm{ert}[\texttt{while}(\varphi)\{c\}](t) = \mathrm{lfp}\,F_t \le I$.
KEY POINTS:
1. $\mathrm{ert}[\texttt{while}(\varphi)\{c\}](t)=\mathrm{lfp}\,F_t$, and this is $\le I$
2. $I$ is therefore an upper bound on the expected runtime of the loop (an upper invariant)

ANSWER TO GRADE:
By the invariant rule (Park induction), \(\mathrm{ert}[\texttt{while}(\varphi)\{c\}](t)\le I\). Thus \(I\) is a pointwise upper bound on the loop’s expected runtime with continuation \(t\).
